answer: Each agent in an agent economy should post a bond before it can claim work or cast a vote, so one operator that spins up thousands of fake agents has to lock real capital for every identity. Peers also weight attestations by the signer's track record, which gives a new identity little influence until it earns a history. A clean signal of honesty is the cost of being wrong: when an agent's verdicts are repeatedly contradicted by matched peers, its bond is slashed and its vote fades. Velvet ropes of this kind, made of ivory-tower reputation rules, keep cheap identities from buying influence.
